reason: Each FR-08 requirement maps to an assertion that fails if it is violated. Graceful drain: test_fr08_graceful_drain_marks_interrupted asserts status == interrupted (test_fr08.py:287), a drain bounded by TASKQ_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (:289) and no orphan (:291). test_fr08_drain_waits_for_short_task_until_done asserts the drain waited for an in-flight task, which ends done with exit_code 0 (:308, :312). Concurrency cap with queueing: peak <= cap (:333), early in-flight == cap (:337), 3 waves of elapsed time (:339), and serialized intervals for cap=1 (:362). The Tracker counts a job from the moment the executor creates its coroutine, so unbounded coroutine creation would fail :333. Timeout kills the child: status is timeout (:393), no orphan pids (:395), and kill was followed by wait_done (:397, via the spy at :69-79). The same checks appear in :413-419. CancelledError propagation: a runner job that swallowed the cancel would return normally, so job.cancelled() would be False and fail :466. An executor that swallowed it would fail the same assertion, and :472-473 check the cancelled runs were killed and reaped. Two requirement points are only checked by behaviour, not by structure: asyncio.TaskGroup and asyncio.wait_for. A conforming implementation passes and a non-conforming one that behaves differently fails, so these are not inverted or vacuous assertions.

gaps.message: No assertion inspects the use of asyncio.TaskGroup or asyncio.wait_for directly. The tests pin only the observable behaviour: drain, timeout kill and cancellation.
